newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Sexwale to quit politics for business.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Sexwale to quit politics for business.

text.p: Tokyo Sexwale is to step down as Premier of South Africa's Gauteng Province in January 1998 to pursue a career in the private sector, the African National Congress (ANC) said on Thursday.
ANC Provincial Secretary-General Paul Mashatile told reporters the executive committee had accepted Sexwale's resignation at a meeting on June 11.
Sexwale would continue to be chairman of the ANC in Gauteng until the end of 1998 and would continue to play a prominent role in the affairs of the party.
There has been widespread speculation that Sexwale, one of the most popular leaders in the ANC, might be planning to join mining house JCI Ltd, now chaired by old friend Mzi Khumalo.
But Sexwale denied this was the case. He said he had received several proposals but had not taken any definite decisions about his future.
"One will cross the bridge when one arrives," he told the news conference.

The provincial leadership of the ANC and its allies in the South African Communist Party, the Congress of South African Trade Unions and the South African National Civics Organisation would hold a joint meeting in July to receive proposals on his successor as premier.
The name of the new premier would be announced in August, Mashatile said.
